metadata.topic: Mechanics — Definition of Period of a Simple Pendulum
metadata.note: 2m: define period of a simple pendulum. 2-slot cloze: 'time(1m) / one complete oscillation(1m)'. Key discriminator: 'one complete oscillation/swing' not 'half swing' (a to b only = half period).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q1a — Define Period of a Simple Pendulum
question.text:
Define the period of a simple pendulum by completing the statement below:

The period of a simple pendulum is the [[1]] taken for the pendulum to complete [[2]].
question.general_feedback:
Period of a simple pendulum:

The period (T) is the time taken for the pendulum to complete one complete oscillation (one full swing — from A to B and back to A).

Key points:

  • A 'complete oscillation' = back and forth = from one extreme, to the other extreme, and back to the starting position.
  • Half a swing (A to B only) = half a period — a common error.
  • SI unit of period: seconds (s).
  • Related: frequency f = 1/T (Hz).

ddwtos.cloze_html: The period of a simple pendulum is the [[1]] taken for the pendulum to complete [[2]].

groups.label: Period is the ___ taken for...
groups.diagnostic_hint: Period is measured in TIME (seconds). It answers "how long does one oscillation take?" — a duration, not a distance or frequency.

groups.label: Period is the time taken for ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: ONE COMPLETE OSCILLATION (or one complete swing). A "complete swing" means the bob travels from start → one extreme → the other extreme → back to start. Half a swing is only half a period.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 8 tokens for 2 slots. Slot 1 (time): 'distance' is unrelated to the definition of period. 'Frequency' is the reciprocal of period (f = 1/T) — students who confuse frequency with period select this. 'Speed' is irrelevant. Slot 2 (one complete oscillation/swing): both accepted. 'Half a swing' is the critical trap — swinging from the rest position to one extreme = one quarter period; extreme to extreme = half period. 'Ten oscillations' describes a technique for averaging timing (time 10 oscillations then divide) but is not the definition.
